emails.subject: TONIGHT - Transgender Day of Remembrance Community Gathering @5pm
emails.body_text:
Transgender Day of Remembrance Community Gathering & Display
Tonight, November 6th | RSVP for Location | 5-7pm
Join OPAL on Thursday evening in a gathering space for reflection, grief, & community to honor Transgender Day of Remembrance. TDOR<https://glaad.org/tdor/> intends to draw awareness to violence against the Trans community and honor the memories of those we have lost. All students, faculty, and staff are welcome.
Click here to RSVP<https://forms.gle/jS6HFNRzsbrYXEjw8>
Can't make it but want to learn more about TDOR? Visit the Trans Flag display on the lawn in front of Dartmouth Hall, all day on the 6th.

[cid:1664f40f-00ff-4e42-9c44-3ae40507da5a]

[cid:bcf89ef6-075e-4c72-b742-ad6ca27615fd]

✨🔍Transgender History Digital Scavenger Hunt🔎✨
Open now through November 12th!

Participate in a short digital scavenger hunt centering transgender identities and history for a chance to win one of three $25 gift cards! Questions are designed to encourage learning about and appreciation of trans history, and by participating, you will have a chance to engage with trans identities in new and interesting ways. Be sure to check out the answer key once you submit your response to learn even more! Responses will be accepted from November 1st-12th.

[cid:1450b39d-1566-424c-811e-27c812779349]

Additionally, stay tuned for information about the Pride 2026 Committee!

More information about events and opportunities can be found at dartgo.org/qsa<http://dartgo.org/qsa>! We hope to see you soon!
emails.body_html:

Participate in a short digital scavenger hunt centering transgender identities and history for a chance to win one of three $25 gift cards! Questions are designed to encourage learning about and appreciation of trans history, and by participating, you will have a chance to engage with trans identities in new and interesting ways. Be sure to check out the answer key once you submit your response to learn even more! Responses will be accepted from November 1st-12th.



Additionally, stay tuned for information about the Pride 2026 Committee!

More information about events and opportunities can be found at dartgo.org/qsa! We hope to see you soon!

emails.subject: Quant Club: Education session #2 today 🎓
emails.body_text:
There once was a quant with a plan,

To out-EV the average man,

He calculated the spread,

Used the mean, not his head,

And still blamed the variance when it ran.


This week, we’re continuing the educational series, this time on probability distributions and expected value. A must have set of knowledge for interviews!


📍 ECSC 116
🕢 11/06, 8:00pm


Also reminder to think about participating in Citadel’s to Intercollegiate Stock Pitch Competition 🏆, with the chance for cash prizes, a trip to Harvard, and an interview with Citadel! Apply here<https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSdEaWpLOufk1HaI-3GL9qWGpz68QYfGZIsRc-xjK3kHM2iSSA/viewform>, or See more information here<https://www.harvardfac.org/pitch-competition>. Deadline to submit memos is 11/19.


We expect to see you there.

Dartmouth Quant Club

emails.subject: Monday- practice for challenging holiday conversations!
emails.body_text:
Feeling a bit nervous about heading home for the holidays and talking with family and friends about touchy subjects?  Looking for tips and strategies on how to get through Thanksgiving dinner with that relative who disagrees with everything you say?  Join Dartmouth Dialogues and One Small Step for a dinner workshop that will provide you with the tools you need to enjoy your break and find what is shared with the people who are important to you.

Butter Down the Hatches!  A Pre-Break Dialogue Workshop
Monday, November 10
6pm in Collis 101
Dinner provided!

Register here<https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLScLkjSWBDpAvt46xHNSh_YtonTY-ioJsD7fdLIqoNogRWvGjw/viewform?usp=header>- limited spaces!

emails.from_name: The Federalist Society Student Chapter at Dartmouth College
emails.subject: Flashpoint: Taiwan Strait | Next Monday, November 10, 4-5 PM Rocky 002
emails.body_text:
With geopolitical stability on the decline, one of the major possible flashpoints of conflict is the Taiwan Strait. On Monday, November 10th, Cato Institute Senior Fellow Doug Bandow will be speaking about China's goals with Taiwan, its military capabilities, and how the U.S. should respond to aggression against Taiwan.

This special event is co-hosted by the John Quincy Adams Society at Dartmouth and the Federalist Society Student Chapter at Dartmouth. It will take place from 4-5 PM in Rocky 002 and is open to all. Come with questions!

We look forward to seeing you there!

[cid:b160600d-71b9-4821-86d4-ad828efca790]
